cards.back: The layer of biomolecules adsorbed onto a material in a biological environment.
Measurement of near-surface chemistry, topography, charge, or energy rather than only bulk properties.
The extent to which pores form connected pathways for cell ingress and transport.
The changing share of mechanical support carried by scaffold and newly formed tissue.
The demonstrated capacity of a cell product to produce a defined biological function under specified conditions.
An outcome measuring a tissue or device performance relevant to the intended use.
Appropriate performance with an appropriate host response for a specific application.
A documented process linking requirements, risks, verification, validation, and changes to a device or material.
M = M₀e^(−kt); t½ = ln 2/k; mass loss and stiffness loss follow different curves.
τ ≈ L²/D: halving size cuts time fourfold; mesh size near cargo size slows diffusion.
Bulk: water entry faster than bond cleavage, shape kept then fragmentation. Surface: shrinks from outside.
Diffusion release often ends long before degradation; tethering ties release to degradation and to repair phases.
φ = 1 − ρ*/ρ_s; pore size, interconnection and tortuosity matter as much as porosity.
E*/E_s ≈ (ρ*/ρ_s)²: doubling relative density quadruples stiffness.
Q = k A ΔP/(μ L); permeability rises steeply with pore size.
Check test mode, hydration, strain rate, direction and the tissue reference before accepting a match.
W_a = γ_lv (1 + cos θ); a larger contact angle means a lower work of adhesion with water, and contact angle is only a screening measure for protein adsorption.
Γ = Γ_max C/(K_d + C); coverage = C/(K_d + C), so 90% coverage needs C = 9 K_d and doubling C past saturation adds little.
Γ_max = M/(N_A A) for molar mass M and footprint A; end-on packing holds more mass per area than side-on and changes which parts face the cells.
Diffusion-limited uptake Γ = 2C√(Dt/π) fills a surface in seconds; composition later shifts as higher-affinity proteins displace early arrivers (the Vroman effect).
G = νRT (ν in mol/m³, T in kelvin) and E ≈ 3G for a nearly incompressible gel; Mc = c/ν is the polymer mass per elastically active chain.
ξ ≈ (k_B T/G)^(1/3): the mesh falls only as the cube root of the modulus, so doubling the crosslink density shrinks it by about 21%.
Compare the hydrodynamic radius with ξ; hindrance grows steeply as r_h/ξ approaches 1. Stokes–Einstein: D₀ = k_B T/(6π η r_h).
Cleaving crosslinks lowers G and enlarges ξ, so an untethered cargo is released more readily even while most of the mass remains.
p = 1 − e^(−kt) is the fraction of bonds cleaved; 1/Mn = 1/Mn0 + p/M_u, so a few percent of bonds cleaved can cut the chain length by a large factor.
Mass is lost only when fragments are small enough to dissolve (M_crit); t_c = −ln(1 − p_crit)/k with p_crit = M_u (1/M_crit − 1/Mn0).
Compare the diffusion time L²/D with the reaction time 1/k; the critical thickness is L_c = √(D/k). Thinner devices erode in bulk, thicker ones more from the surface.
Use molar mass, mass and mechanical tests together; mass lags chain scission, and buffer rate constants are starting estimates for tissue.
Hoop stress σ = PR/h for a thin tube (P in pascals; 1 mmHg = 133.3 Pa); strain = σ/E. Thinner or wider walls carry more stress.
P_cr = E/(4(1 − ν²)) × (h/R)³; halving the thickness lowers P_cr eightfold, and P_cr falls in proportion to E as the wall degrades.
At fixed pressure drop Q ∝ r⁴, so a 20% loss of radius leaves 41% of the flow; wall shear τ = 4μQ/(πr³) rises by 1.95 at fixed flow.
Homogeneous, isotropic, linear-elastic wall, steady Newtonian flow; real vessels are pulsatile and viscoelastic, and shear stress is one input among several.
Relative viability = treated/control × 100; fix the acceptance criterion before the test, and count independent extracts (not wells) as the units.
Average the sections within an animal and compare animals: with 6 per group the t test has 10 degrees of freedom, while counting sections would claim many more.
A capsule of thickness δ and diffusion coefficient D has permeability P = D/δ; flux falls in inverse proportion to thickness, which can disable sensors or cell-containing devices.
Extract tests, animal implants and device tests answer different questions; none shows the response in a person, and a pass is a statement about a use and a test.
N_target = density × volume; N_seed = N_target/η, where η is the fraction of seeded cells that attach and remain.
n = log₂(N_seed/N₀); time = n × t_d (a lower bound); passages = n/log₂(split ratio), rounded up.
Primary cells divide a limited number of times and can change phenotype with expansion, so fewer doublings are better, and a small starting sample is a risk.
Check the volume fraction (cell volume about 2 pL) before seeding a target number; the independent unit for a claim is the donor, not wells from one donor.
Count the specimens and average each measurement at each time point; the specimen is the unit.
p = M_u (1/Mn − 1/Mn0); k = −ln(1 − p)/t. A percent or two of bonds cleaved can reduce the molar mass by an order of magnitude.
For exponential decay, t½ = ln 2/k with k = ln(E₀/E)/t; the time to a threshold is ln(E₀/E_min)/k.
Molar mass and modulus change before mass; judge support from a mechanical or chain-length measure, and treat buffer rates as starting estimates for tissue.
Area ∝ r², flow at fixed pressure ∝ r⁴ and wall shear at fixed flow ∝ r⁻³: a 22% loss of radius removes 39% of the area, 63% of the flow and more than doubles the shear.

Mechanical collapse (flattened lumen, thin or soft wall), chemical injury (local pH, products tracking degradation) and biological response (round lumen with tissue inside) predict different observations.
A matched slow- or non-degrading scaffold separates degradation from geometry and surgery; a sham group sets the baseline; assessment is blinded and the animal is the unit.
Pre-specify the function (flow or patency) as the primary end point; geometry, chemistry and histology explain it, and a threshold calculation shows possibility, not occurrence.
